title: Potassium

review.note: Drafted from the source below; not yet reviewed by a medical professional.

measures: A potassium blood test measures the amount of potassium in your blood. Potassium is an electrolyte that your cells, nerves, heart, and muscles need to work properly.
context: You usually get most of the potassium you need from food, and the kidneys remove extra potassium in urine. A result outside the normal range does not always mean a condition that needs treatment; certain medicines and supplements can raise levels, and clenching your fist during the blood draw can temporarily raise the reading.
aboveRange: Injuries, burns, or surgery that release potassium from cells
Type 1 diabetes that is not well controlled
Side effects of certain medicines, such as water pills or antibiotics
belowRange: Side effects of prescription water pills
Fluid loss from diarrhea, vomiting, or heavy sweating
A kidney condition or heavy alcohol use
nextStep: Discuss this result with your doctor.
